# Spiritual Translation of the Chapter

---

**¶1. ** All these incomplete and ab ortive spiritual forms — among them blind self -intelligence and its consort, the perv erted will, together with the fals ities they served — these are the powers that fash ioned the earliest human will and understanding. Yet how did they discover the Divine Human form impressed upon the consciousness they shaped , when , at the time the Divine was revealed to the governing powers above them , these ab ortive forms did not yet exist? They never perceived Divine Truth made manifest. And yet the im print of the Divine form was somehow transferred into the will and understanding they fash ioned, as though a seal had been set there by a hand they never saw.

---

**¶2.** The evil that p oured forth from self -derived states of intelligence — which is to say, falsity in its gross and material aspect — rose up and directed itself against the appearance of Divine Truth. It was sev ered from that higher rational plane and descended into the natural mind, for it was not received among the ordering tru ths of the rational faculty . When it came down into the external natural mind, it organized itself into a system of perverted perception . It ro oted itself in merely natural knowledge and produced from that knowledge its own works . And when the abortive spiritual forms likewise fell into the natural mind a second time…

---

**¶3. ** … within those evil works, the fals ity took possession of them and spoke through the chief governing principle of self-intelligence. It says to its companion fac ulties: * Surrender to me your understanding , and I will fashion for you a semblance of the Divine — a counterfeit form after the pattern of what is highest . * What it commanded , they performed : they yiel ded their understanding, and it constructed a count erfeit lik eness.

---

**¶4. ** The evil that p oured forth from self -derived states — the fals ity that had perceived the out ward appearance of Divine Truth and from that perception organized a false system of knowledge , ro oting itself within it — afterward this evil rose up within the works produced by that false knowledge. It entered into the self -derived governing states of the natural mind; through those evil works it took possession of them , and they in turn formed the human will and understanding after a count erfeit lik eness of the Divine. Through the active force of that evil which had once glimp sed the appearance of Divine Truth, it penet rated the self-derived fac ulties by means of the works they consumed . It assumed them, and they in turn shaped each human faculty according to its own hered itary disposition — some faculties ret aining a resemblance to the Divine form, others losing the resemblance entirely .

---

**¶6 .** The form ative power arranged within the will and understanding both external and internal faculties, suited for both perception and activity, ordered degree by degree in discrete arrangement . For everything that the per cept ive and ele mental faculties receive from without , there exist corresponding interior memories , repositories , and hidden rec esses within ; and whatever is received into these is retained there . Whenever the interior faculties are called upon to give account of what has been depos ited within their memories , they bring forth what they have received and present it to the inqu iring intelligence that sought it from them.

---

**¶ 7 .** In this way the faculty of perception extends through the outer fac ulties to perce ive every kind and quality of thing within its reach .

---

**¶8. ** The faculty of intellectual sight likewise poss esses its own interior memories , rec esses, repositories , and stores within , so that every form it may perce ive — whether from good or from evil, whether from love or from a version or from desire — it can receive into its memories and repositories . And when the faculty of intellectual sight is moved to send forth again the form it perceived and took in, it can enter into its own memories at will, and reflect and search , and it brings that form forth and gives it to the inquiring intelligence that sought it — whether what is sought pert ains to desire , or to an image of love, or to something that rep els. And so that faculty of understanding produces and acts according to each kind of content .

---

**¶9 .** The faculty of obedient reception — the hearing of truth — possesses its own memories also . Every communication it receives, whether from good or from evil, is taken in and placed within its interior repositories, and is preserved there through long states of spiritual duration . After such extended time, if an inqu iring intelligence comes and asks this faculty about what it heard at a particular time and stored within its memories , immediately it enters into its repositories and searches , reviews , and traces that communication , and sends it forth from where it was first placed, the interior re cess in which it was kept .

---

**¶10. ** In like order , the faculty of perce iving interior spiritual quality functions just as that of intellectual sight and that of ob edient reception. Every quality of spiritual state it disc erns, it takes into itself and deposits in its interior memories . Whenever it is called upon by an inquiring intelligence, it enters its own repositories and rememb ers — though it pert ains only to the things proper to that faculty.

---

**¶11. ** Moreover , the faculty of out ward expression and communication, together with the capacity for disc ernment and appropriation dwelling within it — this too poss esses rec esses and repositories set apart for it. It receives what it has disc erned and g athers these within . And at any moment when an inquiring intelligence seeks after a particular quality of what was appropri ated, it sends it forth and remembers that disc ernment. It captures and renders even the distingu ishing character of what was t asted and appropri ated, giving its memory to whatever intelligence asks for it.

---

** ¶12.** Likewise , the faculty of experi ential contact — the most external knowing by direct encounter — functions in the same manner: when it touches anything in experience , it receives the memory of that contact . And it holds it in its interior repository until an inquiring intelligence asks this faculty for that memory. Immediately it enters again within and brings forth the memory of the experience it made , and gives it to whatever intelligence asks.

---

**¶13. ** And the faculty of the will , which rules over them all, is far more abund antly end owed in this way than any other . Everything that these five per ceptive faculties receive and deposit for the will , the will receives and guards . At any time the fac ulties request what they have ent rusted to it , the will sends forth and rest ores everything that was given to it.

---

** ¶14.** For the counsel of the will is like the sovereign . All the deliber ative principles of its domain and the leading powers of its ordered life are placed under it . At any time these governing powers entr eat it for whatever they need , the will provides the counsel and determination by which they act .

---

**¶15. ** Furthermore, the will is like a ste ward of an interior stor ehouse: everything that is entrusted to it by the faculties, and given into its keeping , it receives and places in separate containing forms and ordered arrangements . At any time…

---

**¶16. ** …in the arrangement where it placed each thing.

---

**¶17. ** This also is the manner of the governing faculty of the whole external person . The perception that intellectual sight has seen and given to it, which it receives in wardly — it brings forth again from the memories where it had placed it, and gives it to whatever intelligence asks for it.

---

**¶18. ** Likewise, the communication that the faculty of ob edient reception heard and gave to it, which it received from that faculty — at any time when an inquiring intelligence asks for that communication, it brings it forth and gives what was heard to whatever intelligence has asked. It brings forth and gives what was received through ob edience to whoever has asked.

---

**¶ 19.** The faculty of perce iving spiritual quality follows the same pattern; and that of disc ernment and appropriation is of the same kind . Experi ential contact likewise : they bring it forth… and whenever the inquiry is made, it brings it forth and gives it .

---

**¶20. ** Indeed, there are guardian aff ections stationed at each of these open ings of the mind, gu arding them, and restra ints are fast ened upon the mind 's entr ances under the authority of the aff ections that guard them.

---

**¶21. ** Just as guardian aff ections guard an ordered spiritual domain with elevated states and watch ful principles — and as the passages lead from there and the restra ints are upon the entr ances — the governing aff ections control what opens and closes the mind's gates while they d well at the threshold of each watch ful principle. So , whatever acc ords with the mind's ruling love, being as a fellow citizen of its own spiritual country, for this they open the entrance and will ingly receive it within . However , whatever is foreign and does not belong to the mind's ruling love, they prevent and leave standing at the threshold . They do not yield to let it enter . Yet there is also that which is received only with great difficulty and deliber ation — for the passages are many and the restraints are numerous . Whenever someone poss essing authority over the restra ints wishes, he opens the entrance and brings forth whatever is hidden within.

---

**¶ 22.** The external person is like a great fort ified spiritual domain . And the entr ances of that domain with their guard ians are like the open ings and organs of the mind — the fac ulties of intellectual sight, of obedient reception, of perce iving spiritual quality, and of expressing what is within . There are many vigil ant principles and a great number of guardian affections stationed over the particular fac ulties of the external person, watching over its open ings. And the governing faculty within is the directing principle of the whole person , the sovereign of the entire spiritual domain — so that when it w ills, it can open, and when it wills, it can close.

---

**¶ 23.** However , when Divine Wisdom desc ends and approaches the open ings of the external person, the self -derived governing states — the guard ians of the entrances — h inder it and resist its entry. They bind shut the whole circuit of the external person so that this stranger — this infl ux from beyond the self — cannot enter.

---

**¶24. ** Nevertheless , Divine Wisdom through its own intelligence , its holy a we , and its tir eless persistence hum bles the self -derived guard ians stationed at the mind 's open ings. When it has finished subd uing them, it takes from them the restra ints to every opening of the external person. Now, those open ings which had formerly stood wide to the proc essions of sel fish desire — receiving in the del ights of conc upiscence, transm itting the pre occupations of world ly life , taking in the pleas ures of bod ily appetite and un cl ean ind ulgences together with the evil inher ent in them — whoever ce ases to receive these things , his will and his understanding turn away from them and follow after the Divine .

---

**¶25. ** So now , because the restra ints over the whole external person of the one under going regener ation are in the hands of Divine Wisdom within , he is opened to receive all that is ple asing to the Lord . He is opened to take in through his understanding the per ceptions of love and righte ousness.

---

**¶26. ** Likewise , the faculty of ob edient reception, which formerly opened itself to empty fals ities and to the enticements of sel fish desire and to the hidden counsel s of wick edness — all of which once gave pleasure at the time they were received — now, by the power of Divine Wisdom, the enticements of self -love and the persu asions of cun ning and evil mysteries have become loathsome in the regener ating person 's perception , so that he has no desire to receive them from this time forward .

---

**¶27 .** Simply stated : all the open ings of the mind in like manner were at one time opened to evil , but have now been opened to good. Evil was ruling in the external person during that former time, doing whatever it w illed, with no higher authority to restrain it.

---

**¶28. ** Yet now , authority has been taken from evil in every faculty of the external person. The Lord 's own Life has become sovereign over all the person 's faculties. It has bound them with a bond of heav enly peace , and confirmed them with the seal of Divine Truth. It has opened every entrance of the external person to what is good , and because of this, good enters through ob edient reception and through understanding alike . It dw ells in the will . ✦

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: All [these a]bortions, amongst them are Saklas and his consort and the ones whom they have served [in the darkness], they are the ones that shaped Adam and Eve. How did they find this beautiful image laid over their shape, even though when it was displayed to their fathers they were not in existence? They never saw the image of the Ambassador! And how did they take the seal of the image of the Ambassador? They added it to [the] shape of Adam and Eve.

[in the] fruits, it assumed the[m] and spoke in the ruler, their leader. He says to his companions: Come! Give me your light, and I will construct for you an image aft[er] the likeness of the exalted one. What he said, they did: they gave it to him, and he constructed [the image of Adam and Eve after the form of the exalted one].

Again the enlightener says: The Sin that s[purted out from the rulers and shot up to the heavens,] which is the Matter that saw the im[age of the Ambassa]dor and that formed the tre[e and was established i]n [i]t; afterwards it came up in the [fruits of the tree]. It went in to the rulers [and assumed them, and] they formed Adam and Eve after the [likeness of the] exalt[ed one]. Through the energy of the Sin that had s[een the image of the] Ambassador, it went into the (rulers) [through the fruits. It] assumed them and they [t]oo sculp[ted the form of Adam and Eve. And they] begat each of them according to his destiny [and his likeness]; one he resembles, one he does not resemble.

The moulder placed in the form of Adam and Eve limbs, outside and within, for perception and activity. He was apportioned house by house. For everything that his perceptions and elements will receive externally there are internal storehouses and repositories and cavities; and what is received in to them is stored in them. Whenever they will be questioned about what is deposited in their internal storehouses, they bring out what they have received within and give it to the questioner who requested it of them.

The faculty of the ears has its own storehouses also. Every sound it might receive, whether good or evil, shall be taken in and placed in its houses and inner repositories, and it is guarded in its [inner recesses] for a thousand days. After a thousand days, if someone comes and asks that faculty about the sound that it heard [at] this time and took into its storehouses, immediately it [sh]all g[o] into its repositories and seek and review and search after this word, and send it out from where it was first put, the place in which it was kept.

[In] like order, the faculty of scent [s]hall function just as that of the eyes and that of the auditory organs. Every [o]dour it shall smell it shall take in [to it] and [d]eposit in its inner storehouses. Every time it will be [a]sked by a questioner, it shall go in [to its cavities] and [search its] storehouse and remember [and bring forth] only these things.

However, even the mouth and the tongue within it, and the taste organ, have a faculty dwelling in them. Again, that faculty too, of taste, has thus cavities and repositories set apart for it. It too receives these tastes and gathers them in. A[nd] at any moment when someone will ask of a taste, if [it has been stored in its repositories,] it shall send it out and remember tha[t] taste. It shall snare and give even the mar[k of] th[a]t taste; give its memory to the qu[est]ioner who asks for it.

Again, the fac[ul]ty of touch by the hands is also s[o]: When it might touch, touch shall [receive i]ts memory. And it [takes] it in to its inner repository [until] som[eo]ne will ask this faculty for the memory. [Immediately], it shall go in again and bring out the memory of this touch that it made, and give it to whoever asks for it.

And the faculty of the heart that rules over them all is much the most like this. Every thing that these five faculties will receive and put in store for the faculty of the heart it shall receive and guard. Any time that they will ask for their deposit it shall send out and give every thing that they gave to it.

For the counsel of the heart is like the king. All the ad[v]isers of his city and the leaders of his a[r]my are placed with him. Any time if his genera[ls] will entreat him for whatever they wish, he shall give them the ad[v]ice and opinion by which they move.

Furthermore, it is like a cellarman: [Eve]ry thing that will be entrusted to it by them, and given to it, it shall receive and put in separate vessels and places. Any time [they shall come and ask the cellarman for what they deposited with it, it shall go in to its vessels and seek and find every thing that was given to it, and bring it out and give it to the one who asked for it.]
[Every thing it shall find] in the place that it put it.

This also is the way of the faculty of the body. The vision that the eyes will see and give to it, and it receives it in, it shall bring out again from the storehouses wherein it had placed it; and give it to whoever asks for it.

Again, [the] sound that the ears will hear and give to it, and it receives it from them. At any time when someone will ask it for that sound, it shall bring out and give the sound of the ears to whoever has asked it for that sound. It shall bring out and give the sound of the ears to whoever has asked.

Again, [the] faculty of smell in this same pattern; and that of taste is of the same [ty]pe. The touch by the han[ds is also of this same type. Every touch it receives, it shall take in to its inner storehouses. And] they shall bring it out in to [the one who requests it of them.] And whenever they will as[k it] for it, it shall bring it out and gi[ve it].
Indeed, watchmen are a[t] these doors guarding them, and bolts are fastened on the doors at the hands of the guards that guard them!

Just like watchmen guarding a camp with towers and watch-posts. As the holding rooms come out from there and the bolts are upon the gates, the guards control the bolts of the gates while they sit at the entrance [of] the watchposts. So, someone who belongs to their city as a fellow [cit]izen of them, belonging to their country, for him they shall open [the ga]te and receive him in by their will. However, the foreigner who comes they shall prevent, and leave him standing at the gate. They shall not yield to let him enter. Again, another one whom they will receive in, with great trouble before [they] take him in, you shall find many holding rooms [and passages and inner chambers] that [are set between them, and] there are a mass [of bolts and locks placed upon] them. The number of d[oor] bolts [upon the gates] are [past counting.] Whenever someone will wish [to open them, he who holds] the bolts at his hand, opens the gate and brings out whoever is hidden within.

This body too is like the mighty camp. And the gates of the camp with their guards are like the orifices and organs of the body. Now, the orifices of the body are of sight, hearing and smell; and they that send out words. There are many sentinels and a mass of guards placed over the limbs of the body, guarding their orifices. And the faculty in it is the directive of the body, the queen of the entire camp; so that whenever it wishes it can open, or when it wishes it can shut.

However, if and wh[en] the Light Mind comes, it shall tu[rn i]n to the orifices of the body. The rulers, who [a]re the door gua[rds], shall h[in]der and restrain it from en[ter]ing. They shall bind the circu[it] of the body so that the foreign[er] can not enter it.

Nevertheless, the Light Mind by its wisdom and awe and diligence shall hum[ble] the guards who are set at the body's orifices. When it finishes humbling them it shall take fr[o]m them bolts to all the orifices of the body. Now, the orifices that had been opened before to the parades of Lust, to receive in the sights of pleasure, to transfer the [wor]ds of the practice of li[f]e's concerns, to receive in the t[astes] of the different foods and unclean meals together with the Sin therein; whoever stops receiving th[is] in, his heart and mind shall follow after.

So, now, bec[ause] the b[olt]s to the body of the righteous person are in the hands of the Light M[in]d within, he is open [to receive] in all that is pleasing to God. He is op[en to take] in by his eyes the visions of lov[e and truth] and righteousness. Yet, now, by the power of the Light Mind that has suffused him and lived in the body he has humbled Lust, the goddess of the body. The parades of Lust have become loathsome in the presence of the righteous person. How-ever, the aspects of divinity and righteousness and humility and scorned clothes are pleasing to him.

[S]imply, all orifices in similar fashion were opening at one time to wickedness, but now have opened to the good. Sin was ruling in the body this time, doing anything it liked, having none in command.

Yet, [n]ow, authority has been taken from the Sin in the org[ans] of the body. The Living Spirit has become lord over all its limbs. It has bound them with a chain of peace, and sealed them with the seal of truth. It has opened the orifices of the body to the good, and because of this the good enters them through the ears and the eyes. It dwells in the heart. The H[o]ly Spirit reigns. It does all that it pleases. It annuls [the] will of [S]in, the begin-ning and the end. [However], the will of the [Holy Spir][it] comes about, and the purpose of the Light Mind.
In this way his faculty [extends through the] outer [limbs] to look at [and perceive] every type with [in its reach.]

Also [the fa ]culty of the eyes [has ] houses and cavities and repositories and stores within, so that every image it might see, whether good or evil, whether loveable or detestable or lustful, it can receive into its storehouses and repositories. Also, when the faculty of the eyes is pleased to send out the image that it saw and took in, it can go in to its storehouses [at the ] time and think and seek [and review and search after this image,] and it brings it out [and] gives it to the questioner who requested it and the one who wan[t ]ed it—whether it be something from lu[st and desire, or a]n image of love [or an image of something] hateful. And thus shall that faculty (of the eyes) produce and do what it does in each category.

The enlightener [speak]s to them thus: The Sin that spurted out from the rulers, which is Matter, shot up [tow]ards the image of the Ambassador. It was cut off from [tha]t place and came down to the earth, for they did not accept [it wi]thin the firmaments. When it came do[wn to] the earth, it formed the tree. It was established within the wood and formed the fruits. And when [the] abortions fell [to] the ground, to the earth, at the [second] time [ ... / ... ]
